findings.claim: IEC 61851-1 sub-clause 8.4 states that for Modes 3 and 4 'protective earthing conductors shall not be switched'; the UK has a national derogation (BS 7671 722.411.4.1) allowing open-PEN devices to disconnect PE.
findings.detail: BEAMA paper 'Protective earth disconnection when carrying out EV charging' quotes 8.4 verbatim. Ecoharmony/Zaptec UK pages confirm IEC 61851-1 does not permit interrupting PE and that the UK implemented a local derogation. Consequence for the test switchboard: opening the DUT's PE is a TEST-MODE-ONLY function, never part of a normal installation.

findings.claim: IEC/HD 60364-5-54:2011 clause 543.3.3: no switching device shall be inserted in the protective conductor; only joints that can be disconnected for test purposes by use of a tool are permitted (plus plug/socket connections of class I equipment).
findings.detail: This is why a PE-fault simulator is legitimate only as electrical test equipment (EN 50191), with a tool/key-enabled test mode, and never as a fixed-installation feature. PN-HD 60364-5-54 is the Polish adoption.

findings.claim: EN 50191 (DIN EN 50191:2011-10 / VDE 0104) 'Erection and operation of electrical test equipment' is the applicable standard for a bench/switchboard that deliberately produces hazardous conditions (test benches, test areas, non-stationary test installations); a 2026 draft revision exists.
findings.detail: Metrel publishes a 'Guide working place according to EN 50191' (PDF). Typical EN 50191 measures (from the standard's scope, exact clauses not retrievable): test station with/without automatic protection against direct contact, emergency-stop, red/green signal lamps, key switch, barriers, qualified-person operation. The fault switchboard should be documented as an EN 50191 test installation, not as a PN-HD 60364 distribution board.

findings.claim: BS 7671 722.411.4.1(iv) open-PEN device: trips when L-N utilisation voltage is >253 V rms or <207 V rms for more than 5 s and disconnects all live conductors AND the PE from the supply within 5 s.
findings.detail: 207/253 V = 230 V -10%/+10%. Zaptec Go UK O-PEN version and PlugStream/Ecoharmony installer pages give the same numbers. Option (iii) of 722.411.4.1 (PE-to-true-earth > 70 V via earth electrode) is recalled from the regulation but was not confirmed by a retrieved source.

findings.claim: IET Wiring Matters (July 2023) warns that cable voltage drop on long EV circuits can push the L-N voltage at the charge point below the 207 V threshold under load, causing nuisance O-PEN trips – i.e. undersized/long cable and under-voltage detection interact.
findings.detail: Article title: 'How voltage drop can affect EV charging point open PEN detection devices'. Full text could not be fetched (proxy blocked). Useful demo: combine the 'undersized cable' resistor with 32 A load to show a 207 V-type trip.

findings.claim: IEC 61851-1:2017 test reports specify the mains supply tolerance for EVSE as ±10 % of rated voltage (i.e. 207–253 V at 230 V); the standard itself does not define mandatory under/over-voltage trip thresholds.
findings.detail: Figure taken from a published IEC 61851-1:2017 CB test report snippet; exact clause number not retrieved. Practical wallbox windows (Easee, UK O-PEN devices) coincide with 207–253 V; Wallbox (brand) uses a much lower under-voltage error threshold (<150 V, error #112).

findings.claim: IEC 62955:2018 RDC-DD must detect smooth residual DC ≥ 6 mA and remove supply so an upstream Type A/F RCD is not impaired; maximum break time at 6 mA is 10 s; Table 2 also specifies break times at 60 mA and 200 mA.
findings.detail: Bender RDC104 datasheet: commissioning check must use IEC 62955 Table 2 trip times at 6/60/200 mA. Values of 300 ms (60 mA) and 100 ms (200 mA) are recalled, NOT confirmed by retrieved text. RDC-PD variant combines 6 mA DC detection with 30 mA Type A/F protection and isolates contacts. Smooth DC above ~6 mA can reduce or eliminate a Type A RCD's ability to trip.

findings.topic: Standards – RCD Type A trip behaviour (IEC 61008)
findings.claim: Type A RCD: no trip at 0.5 IΔn, must trip ≤300 ms at 1 IΔn, ≤40 ms at 5 IΔn; pulsating-DC test current is half-wave rectified with 1.4× multiplier (so 42 mA pulsating for a 30 mA device); Type A tolerates up to 6 mA smooth DC.
findings.detail: Hence: 6 mA smooth DC injected downstream of a wallbox trips the wallbox RDC-DD but NOT a Type A upstream; a half-wave 6 mA pulse also will not trip Type A (needs ≥ ~42 mA). Type AC trips on neither. Fluke KA-01292 and IPD technical page.

findings.claim: PN-HD 60364-7-722 requires each EV connection point to be individually protected by an RCD IΔn ≤ 30 mA of at least Type A (with 6 mA DC detection, RDC-DD) or Type B, plus its own overcurrent device (dedicated circuit); Type AC is not acceptable; SPD protection is required for publicly accessible charging points (722.443).
findings.detail: Sources: elektro.info.pl (two articles), kanalelektryczny.pl, greenkick, e-elektryczna.pl (ochrona przepięciowa). Most frequent Polish error: Type A RCD installed without confirming the wallbox contains an RDC-DD 6 mA. Polish version cited: PN-HD 60364-7-722:2019-03.

findings.claim: IEC/HD 60364-5-52 Annex G: recommended max voltage drop 3 % (lighting) and 5 % (other uses) for installations fed from public LV network; 6 %/8 % for private LV supply.
findings.detail: 5 % of 230 V = 11.5 V. Used as the pass/fail reference for the 'undersized conductor' demo.

findings.claim: Wallboxes detect loss of installation PE mainly by (a) measuring N-PE (and L-PE) voltage/impedance – a floating PE shows abnormal N-PE voltage or too-high L-N/L-PE relation, (b) 'PEN-fault' voltage-window logic (207/253 V), and (c) at the EV side via the CP/PP circuit whose return path is PE (patents: PE loss detected from the PP DC level dropping to ≤40–60 %, charging stopped within 30 ms).
findings.detail: CP-only monitoring can miss an open PE because CP return current then flows through the PP resistors in the connector, so PP monitoring is added (WO2019211233A1 / US 11,933,862). go-e: 'Erdungsprüfung' blocks charging in TN/TT grids with insufficient earth, enabled by default, can be disabled in the app for IT grids (Norway); 4 red LEDs at 3/6/9/12 o'clock indicate the disabled state. Wallbox-brand troubleshooting: charger detects too-high resistance/voltage between L1 and N when PE is disconnected.

findings.claim: Easee stops charging if supply <207 V or >253 V and auto-resumes when voltage is stable in window; Wallbox (Pulsar) error #112 'Undervoltage' when L1-N <150 V; Wallbox error 09 = phase loss/imbalance; go-e E03 = phase loss/imbalance; Mercedes E12, BMW E13 = phase loss; Alfen: when set to 3-phase on a 1-phase supply reports error 212.
findings.detail: Chargers measure L1-N, L2-N, L3-N and expect 207–253 V. Some 3-phase chargers keep charging after L2/L3 loss with a warning but need a power cycle to return to 3-phase. techfaultfix.com is an aggregator – verify codes against manuals before printing on the HMI.

findings.claim: IEC 61851-1 does not require phase-rotation checking; most wallboxes and EV on-board chargers ignore phase order. Exception: Mennekes AMTRON has a phase-sequence relay requiring a clockwise (right-hand) rotating field; wrong rotation or a missing phase gives Error 10 'installation error'.
findings.detail: Phase order DOES matter for 3-phase meters/DLB CT mapping (CT on wrong phase or reversed = wrong balancing) – an installer error worth simulating for the AC500 DLB. Mennekes installation manual p.33 error table; goingelectric forum thread.

findings.topic: Precedent – commercial EVSE test adapters switch PE in test mode
findings.claim: Metrel A 1532 XA and Kewtech KEWEVSE/KT66 adapters deliberately simulate 'PE open', 'diode short' and 'CP short (state E)' faults and run a 'PE pre-test' (touch-voltage check on PE before connecting); XA version supports 3-phase load test up to 13 A.
findings.detail: This is the industry precedent for switching the DUT's PE inside dedicated test equipment. Output BNC for CP monitoring; banana outputs to a 3-phase installation tester. Price not found.

findings.claim: IEC 62752 IC-CPDs 'check supply conditions and prevent charging in case of supply faults' and 'may have a switched protective conductor' – relevant to testing the P35 portable charger: it is expected to refuse to start on missing PE / L-N swap in TN configuration.
findings.detail: Exact clause text and PE-voltage threshold not retrieved. IEC 62752 Ed.2 2024 exists.

findings.claim: With N open in a 3-phase 4-wire system, the star point floats: loads on two phases share the 400 V line voltage in proportion to their resistances; lightly loaded phase can approach 400 V, heavily loaded phase toward 0 V.
findings.detail: Computed (resistive loads, V1 = 400·R1/(R1+R2)): 1 kW/1 kW → 200/200 V; 1 kW/1.5 kW → 240/160 V; 1 kW/2 kW → 267/133 V; 1 kW/3 kW → 300/100 V; 0.5 kW/2 kW → 320/80 V. A single-phase wallbox simply loses supply; a 3-phase wallbox whose electronics is fed L1-N sees the shifted voltage. Demo needs two unequal auxiliary resistive loads (heaters) on L1-N and L2-N downstream of the N contactor.

findings.topic: Fault physics – N-PE swap / N-PE bridge
findings.claim: Swapping PE and N at a socket/device: with an upstream RCD the circuit trips repeatedly as soon as load current flows (returns via PE); without RCD it 'works' but exposed parts/car body sit at N potential and become 230 V if the N conductor opens.
findings.detail: elektroda.pl thread 'Konsekwencje zamiany przewodu PE z N w gniazdku'. N-PE bridge at the device (TN-C style) splits return current between N and PE by impedance ratio – a 30 mA Type A RCD trips at a few hundred mA of load. Touch voltage on PE equals the N-conductor voltage drop (e.g. 32 A × 0.3 Ω ≈ 10 V). PE conductor must be rated for full load current in these tests (6 mm² available – OK).

findings.claim: Polish sources list as the most frequent wallbox installation errors: connecting to an existing socket/circuit instead of a dedicated circuit; missing or wrong-type RCD (Type AC; Type A without verified 6 mA RDC-DD in the charger); undersized conductor cross-section; no analysis of connection power; no post-installation measurements/protocol; wrong PEN split point / mixing TN-C and TN-S; old installations without PE; missing SPD on public points.
findings.detail: eviacharge.pl, elbud-impex, 3ev.pl PDF, powerbox.ac (two articles, blocked for fetch), elektroda threads 'Błędny podział PEN', 'Spółdzielnia i brak PE'. Not found in sources (own knowledge, flag as unverified): aluminium conductors in copper terminals, wrong torque, shared ('borrowed') neutral between circuits.

findings.claim: A glowing contact (high-resistance copper-oxide junction at a loose screw terminal) reaches >1250 °C at its core (above copper melting point) and can develop with as little as ~0.3 A; heat ∝ I²·R_contact.
findings.detail: Patents US 7,187,529 / US 6,948,846 citing NRIPS research. Justifies the 'burnt contact' demo as a thermal-camera demonstration, but real glowing contacts are an open fire hazard – simulate with a defined power resistor, not a loosened real terminal.

Computed, P = I²R. A continuous 1 Ω at 32 A (1 kW) is impractical in a wall enclosure; practical demo = 0.25–0.5 Ω at 16 A (64–128 W) time-limited, or 0.25 Ω at 32 A (256 W) for ≤10 s. Heatsink for 128 W continuous at ΔT 60 K needs Rth ≤ 0.47 K/W (fan-cooled). Allegro: 100 W 1 Ω aluminium-housed resistors from ~16.85 PLN, 200 W 1 Ω available; 2× 1 Ω/100 W in parallel = 0.5 Ω/200 W, 4× = 0.25 Ω/400 W.

findings.topic: Computation – undersized conductor voltage drop (1-phase, Cu, loop 2L)
findings.detail: Computed with ρ = 0.0175 (20 °C) and 0.0214 Ω·mm²/m (70 °C). To emulate '2.5 mm² × 30 m' in the switchboard insert ~0.42 Ω per conductor (L and N each) or 0.84 Ω in L only; same resistor bank as burnt contact. Alternatively use the buck transformer (-16/-24 V) to mimic the drop with zero heat.

findings.claim: Series secondary carries full load current, so VA = V_sec × I_load: 24 V → 384 VA @16 A / 768 VA @32 A (gives 206/254 V – right on the 207/253 thresholds, too marginal); 30 V → 480 VA @16 A / 960 VA @32 A (200/260 V – clear trip); 40 V → 1280 VA @32 A (190/270 V); 48 V → 768 VA @16 A only.
findings.detail: Computed. Key winding nuance: a '2×24 V 800 VA' toroid has two 16.7 A windings – series (48 V) is only good for 16 A, parallel (24 V) for 33 A. For a 32 A path pick 2×30 V 1000 VA wired in parallel (30 V @ 33 A) or two toroids (e.g. 2×12 V/500 VA + 2×30 V/1000 VA) each with its own polarity changeover → steps ±12/±18/±30/±42 V. Primary current of a 1000 VA unit ≈ 4.3 A. Polarity reversal of the series winding by a 2-pole changeover contactor gives buck or boost; a bypass contactor (shorting the DUT path around the winding, NOT shorting the winding itself) must be closed before any changeover so the load is never fed through an un-energised secondary (magnetising impedance would saturate/drop the voltage).

findings.claim: 500 VA 230 V/2×24 V toroid: Ø136 × 65 mm, 5 kg (ATO). 800 VA 230 V dual secondary: ≈Ø162 × 60 mm, 5.1 kg (Nordtek). 1000 VA: height 70 mm, 6.5 kg (Nordtek) ; Breve TTS1000/D 230/24 V: Ø155 × 82 mm (TME lists 158 × 84 mm), 7.5 kg, secondary 41.7 A, IP00, M6 centre bolt.
findings.detail: Polish makers: Breve Tufvassons (TTS series) and Indel (TST series) – both buyable on Allegro. Allegro prices seen: Indel TST 450/008 2×24 V 487.71 PLN; TST600 24 V 600 VA ≈534 PLN; TST 100/014 2×24 V 202 PLN; a TST 800 variant ≈1007 PLN. Breve TTS1000/D 230/24 V code 17124-9980 (price not captured). For a 3-phase (3 toroid) solution budget ~3 × 7.5 kg = 22 kg and ~3 × Ø160 × 85 mm.

findings.claim: Toroids above ~300 VA draw inrush currents in the order of 100+ A for a few ms and nuisance-trip C-type MCBs; standard fix is an NTC inrush limiter (e.g. CL-90 class) or series resistor in the primary, bypassed by a relay after ~0.5 s.
findings.detail: For the test switchboard: feed each buck/boost primary via its own B/C6 MCB + soft-start (NTC + bypass relay, or a 10–22 Ω/50 W resistor bypassed after 300–500 ms by a Shelly/relay contact). Keep the primary permanently energised during a test session; switch only secondary polarity/bypass.

findings.topic: Hardware – variac vs electronic AC source (alternatives)
findings.claim: Allegro variacs: 5 kVA 260 V 20 A ≈ 2 048.50 PLN; 3 kVA 260 V 12 A 1 821 PLN (250×200×210 mm); 2 kVA 0–250 V ≈ 589 PLN, 4 kg. Electronic programmable AC source: Chroma 61605 4 kVA/300 V list ≈ 16 400 USD (≈10 000 USD clearance), 2 kVA ≈ 8 790 USD.
findings.detail: A 20 A variac covers only a 16 A single-phase path (not 32 A) and needs a motor drive for ESP32 control; a 32 A/3-phase electronic source would be >50 kPLN. The fixed-step buck/boost toroid (±30 V) is the only option that is cheap, controller-switchable and 32 A capable.

findings.claim: Genuine Fotek SSR-40DA: 40 A, on-state drop ≤1 V; widespread counterfeits contain BTA12/BTA16 triacs (12–16 A) – buy a 40 A part for a 16–20 A duty or use a reputable brand; dissipation 1.0–1.6 V × 32 A = 32–51 W per SSR (heatsink mandatory).
findings.detail: Allegro has many 'SSR-40 DA 90-480 VAC' listings (Fotek-style), e.g. offers 5902249141, 6474682729, 7706122642. For random 50–500 ms interruptions use zero-cross SSR driven from ESP32 GPIO (3–32 V DC input); electromechanical contactors (10–30 ms operate time, AC-1 endurance ~10^5 ops) wear out quickly under 32 A chopping. Note: zero-cross SSR chopping produces no arc signature – it will not trigger an AFDD.

findings.claim: Shelly Pro 4PM: 4 relays 16 A each, 40 A total, 96×53×59 mm (3 DIN modules). Shelly Pro 3EM-120A: 3 CTs up to 120 A + N, voltage/current accuracy ±1 % (2–120 A), 94×19×69 mm (1 DIN module).
findings.detail: Fit for the fault lens: Pro 3EM = independent per-phase V/I/power monitor (shows the simulated under/over-voltage, phase loss, imbalance on the HMI via local HTTP/MQTT); Pro 4PM/Plus 1PM = switching of leakage resistors (<1 A) and contactor coils; NOT suitable for 32 A load paths, PE switching (no positively-driven/mirror contacts) or safety interlocks. Per-fault results may be logged via Shelly scripting.

findings.claim: AC leakage from L to PE at 230 V: 6 mA → 38 kΩ (1.4 W); 10 mA → 23 kΩ (2.3 W); 15 mA → 15.3 kΩ (3.4 W); 30 mA → 7.7 kΩ (6.9 W); 60 mA → 3.8 kΩ (13.8 W). Smooth DC via bridge rectifier + smoothing capacitor (≈325 V DC): 6 mA → 54 kΩ (2 W); 10 mA → 32.5 kΩ (3.2 W); 30 mA → 10.8 kΩ (9.8 W).
findings.detail: Computed. Use wirewound resistors rated ≥3× dissipation (e.g. 25 W for the 30 mA AC step), switched by small relays/Shelly channels. Injection point A (downstream of the DUT, i.e. at the Type 2 socket / test plug L→PE): current passes through the wallbox's RDC-DD AND the upstream RCD → 6 mA DC trips only the RDC-DD (≤10 s), 30 mA AC trips both (race). Injection point B (between the switchboard RCD and the DUT input): bypasses the wallbox sensor → demonstrates the upstream RCD alone: Type A trips on 30 mA AC, does not trip on 6 mA smooth DC; Type AC trips on neither pulsating nor smooth DC. 'Blinding' demo: hold 10–30 mA smooth DC at point B, then add 30 mA AC – Type A may fail or trip late; Type B / RDC-DD still trips.

findings.claim: Max Zs for magnetic trip (230 V): B16 2.88 Ω, B32 1.44 Ω, C16 1.44 Ω, C32 0.72 Ω (×0.95 Cmin: 2.73/1.37/1.37/0.68 Ω). With a series PE resistor of 50/100/200 Ω a bolted L-PE fault gives only 4.6/2.3/1.1 A → MCB never trips, only the RCD (<40 ms at 5 IΔn); 40 ms pulse energy in the resistor = 42/21/11 J; max earth resistance for 50 V touch limit with 30 mA RCD = 1 667 Ω.
findings.detail: Computed. A 50–200 Ω, 50 W wirewound resistor inserted in the DUT PE path survives installation-tester loop tests and RCD tests (30 mA × 100 Ω = 3 V) and shows 'TT-like' high Zs on the AmpCheck / installation tester. Never combine the PE-resistor mode with the N-PE bridge or L-PE leakage modes above a few mA (power in the resistor). 1–3 Ω PE resistors (TN loop-limit demos) would see 77–230 A on a real fault → only with low-current tester measurements, interlocked.

findings.topic: Parts – PE / N switching precedent and hardware requirement
findings.claim: To switch the DUT PE or N safely use a contactor whose NC (normally closed) main pole carries PE so that PE is restored on loss of control power (fail-safe), with a positively-driven/mirror auxiliary contact fed back to the controller, coil enabled only through a key switch ('TEST MODE') and a hardware timer; never switch the switchboard's own PE bar – only the single DUT PE conductor.
findings.detail: Design rule derived from IEC 60364-5-54 543.3.3, IEC 61851-1 8.4 and EN 50191 practice; the Metrel/Kewtech adapters show the same 'PE open' switch is acceptable only inside test equipment. Mirror-contact definition: IEC 60947-4-1 Annex F (recalled, not retrieved). Modular NC contactors 25–40 A are available (e.g. 'stycznik modułowy NC' on Allegro) – part numbers to be confirmed by the parts lens.

findings.topic: Fault simulation matrix (per fault: mistake → implementation → expected DUT reaction → hazard/interlock)
findings.claim: PE OPEN: mistake = PE not connected / broken at junction box. Implement: NC contactor pole in DUT PE, key-enabled. Expect: go-e/Easee/Zaptec/UK O-PEN units refuse or stop (N-PE monitoring); plain EVSE without PE monitoring charges normally; the IEC 61851-1 PE-continuity check covers only EVSE→EV cable; upstream RCD still trips on an L→chassis fault but only when current flows (e.g. through a person). Hazard: DUT exposed parts float; interlock = DUT on insulated panel, no-touch rule, 'PE OPEN' red lamp, auto-restore after ≤60 s.
findings.detail: PE HIGH-IMPEDANCE: 50/100/200 Ω 50 W wirewound in PE path (relay-selected). Expect: tester shows high Zs/RA; wallbox usually unaffected; RCD-test still passes. PE LIVE (touch voltage): never connect L to PE directly – feed DUT PE through ≥100 kΩ from L (≤2.3 mA, 0.5 W) or through an isolated 24–50 V/≤10 VA transformer secondary + ≥4.7 kΩ (≤10 mA) in series with the open PE pole; wallbox N-PE monitor (MΩ input) sees 24–230 V and faults; AmpCheck/tester shows PE voltage. Hazard: even 2–10 mA is perceptible – treat as live. N OPEN: 1 NO pole of a 40 A contactor in N; 1-phase DUT dies; 3-phase DUT: add two unequal heaters (e.g. 1 kW L1-N, 2 kW L2-N) downstream → 267/133 V; hazard: DUT overvoltage damage – time-limit ≤5 s, remove SPD, use sacrificial DUT. N-PE SWAP: 2-pole changeover contactor (break-before-make) on DUT N/PE; expect: RCD trips as soon as the DUT draws current; 'no RCD' + swap: works, body at N potential – interlock: swap allowed only when RCD is in circuit. N-PE BRIDGE: 1 relay 16 A N→PE at DUT terminal; expect RCD trip at ~60–100 mA load; without RCD PE carries up to half of 32 A (6 mm² OK). L-N SWAP (1-ph socket): 2-pole changeover; expect EVSE/IC-CPD with N-PE monitoring to refuse ('wiring error'); hazard: single-pole devices leave L connected. PHASE LOSS: NO poles on L2/L3; expect error 09/E03/E12/E13 or 1-phase fallback. WRONG SEQUENCE: two interlocked contactors swapping L2/L3 with ≥50 ms dead time; expect no reaction except Mennekes-type units (Error 10) and wrong DLB/meter per-phase mapping. UNDER/OVER-VOLTAGE: ±30 V series toroid on L1 (200/260 V), optional second ±12 V step; expect Easee-class stop at <207/>253 V after ≤5 s and auto-resume, Wallbox-brand only <150 V; hazard: 260–270 V on DUT electronics – limit to +15 % and ≤30 s. LOOSE CONTACT: zero-cross SSR 40 A (genuine) in L1 with bypass contactor, random 50–500 ms OFF, 0.5–5 s ON; expect EV/EVSE restart or 'relay/mains dropout' error; no AFDD trip. BURNT CONTACT: 0.25/0.5 Ω resistor bank (100 W Al-housed units in parallel) on fan-cooled heatsink with 90 °C bimetal cut-out in the coil circuit + DS18B20/NTC to ESP32, duty ≤60 s @16 A, ≤10 s @32 A, or use buck toroid for heat-free voltage-drop mimic. UNDERSIZED CABLE: same bank at 0.42–0.84 Ω → 5.8–7 % drop vs 5 % Annex G limit. MISSING/WRONG RCD: selectable AC/A/B RCD + bypass via key switch; non-bypassable backstop RCD on the switchboard supply (see recommendations).

recommendations: Classify and label the switchboard as an EN 50191 electrical test installation (not a PN-HD 60364 distribution board): key switch 'TRYB TESTOWY' enabling all PE/N/L manipulation coils, red lamp 'USTERKA AKTYWNA / PE ROZŁĄCZONE', green 'NORMALNY', emergency-stop that drops the main contactor and restores PE, DUT mounted on an insulated panel, signage 'nie dotykać urządzenia podczas testu'.

Switch PE only in the single DUT PE conductor, with the NC pole of a 25–40 A contactor (PE closed when coil de-energised) and a mirror/positively-driven auxiliary contact read by the ESP32; add a hardware watchdog timer (≤60 s) independent of firmware; never switch the enclosure PE bar or the installation PE.

Under/over-voltage: one 230 V/2×30 V 1000 VA toroid (Breve TTS or Indel TST, ~Ø160×85 mm, ~7.5 kg) with the two windings in parallel (30 V @ 33 A) in series with L1, polarity reversed by a 2-pole changeover contactor, plus a bypass contactor around the winding; sequence: bypass ON → changeover → bypass OFF. Optional second toroid 2×12 V 500 VA for ±12/18/42 V steps. Primary via B6 MCB + NTC/resistor soft start (inrush >100 A). Do it on L1 only: wallbox electronics and O-PEN logic are L-N based; three toroids would add ~22 kg and ~3× cost with little demo value.

Burnt contact / undersized cable: build one resistor bank from 4× 1 Ω/100 W aluminium-housed resistors (Allegro ~17 PLN each) on a fan-cooled heatsink (≤0.5 K/W) giving 0.25/0.5/1 Ω by relay selection; protect with a 90 °C bimetal thermostat (KSD301 class) in series with the enabling coil and a DS18B20 to the controller; firmware limits 0.5 Ω to ≤60 s at 16 A and 0.25 Ω to ≤10 s at 32 A; thermal camera visible through a window is the teaching payoff. Use the buck toroid when only the voltage drop (not heat) matters.

Loose contact: genuine zero-cross SSR 40 A (derate to ≤20 A continuous, or use two in parallel/one per phase with heatsinks; 32–51 W loss each) in series with a bypass contactor; firmware generates pseudo-random 50–500 ms gaps with 0.5–5 s ON; limit total chopping time per session; do not advertise it as an AFDD demo (no arc signature).

Earth leakage: resistor ladder 38k/23k/15k/7.7k/3.8k Ω (6/10/15/30/60 mA AC, ≥3× power rating) and DC ladder 54k/32.5k/10.8k Ω after a bridge rectifier + 10–47 µF/400 V capacitor (6/10/30 mA smooth DC); two injection points selectable by relay: A = DUT output (trips wallbox RDC-DD, shows 10 s/6 mA behaviour), B = between RCD and DUT (shows Type AC vs A vs B difference and DC blinding). Shelly Pro 4PM channels (16 A) are adequate to switch these ladders.

RCD selection block: Type AC, Type A, Type B 30 mA in parallel branches with a 4-position break-before-make selector + 'brak RCD' position only via key; keep a NON-bypassable backstop RCD on the switchboard feed – 30 mA Type B if you accept occasional simultaneous tripping during leakage demos, or 100–300 mA Type A/B as fire/backstop with no personal protection (document this choice).

N-PE swap, N-PE bridge, L-N swap, phase loss, phase sequence: use 2-pole changeover modular contactors (AC-1 ≥40 A for L/N paths, 16–25 A for PE bridge) with electrical interlock and ≥50 ms dead time; software interlocks: (a) N-PE swap/bridge allowed only when an RCD is in circuit, (b) PE resistor mode excluded while any L→PE leakage or N-PE bridge is active, (c) N-open with neutral-shift heaters limited to ≤5 s and only with the 'sacrificial DUT' flag set.

Touch voltage on PE: implement only the high-impedance variants (≥100 kΩ from L, or isolated 24–50 V source + ≥4.7 kΩ) so that the worst-case current into a person is ≤2–10 mA; show the result on the AmpCheck / installation tester and on the wallbox fault LED; still treat the DUT as live.

Use the Shellys you have: Pro 3EM (1 module, 120 A CTs, ±1 %) as the independent 'what the installer's meter sees' per-phase monitor on the HMI and for logging each demo; Pro 4PM / Plus 1PM / Pro 1PM relays only for coils and <1 A leakage ladders; Shelly Plus Add-on + DS18B20 for the resistor-bank temperature if you do not want it on the ESP32; do not use Shelly relays in 32 A paths, for PE switching or as safety interlocks.

Add an 'installer mistake' demo specific to the AC500 DLB: CT on wrong phase / reversed CT polarity via a small changeover on the CT secondary (safe, mA level) – this is the DLB error most likely to occur in the field and it costs nothing.

open_questions_for_user: Which Shelly models and how many (Pro 3EM, Pro 4PM, Plus 1PM, Pro 1PM, Add-on, Uni)? This decides metering vs relay roles.

Will people be able to touch the DUT (training room) during PE-open / N-PE swap demos, or is it a hands-off demo behind a window? This decides whether a 30 mA Type B backstop RCD is mandatory on the feed.
Are the DUTs (WB500, P35) sacrificial engineering units? Over-voltage (260–270 V) and neutral-shift (300 V+) tests can damage electronics.
Do you need a real thermal (I²R) burnt-contact demo for a thermal camera, or is a voltage-drop mimic via the buck toroid enough? (Saves ~400 W heat, heatsink and fan.)
Is under/over-voltage on L1 only acceptable, or do you need all three phases (adds ~2× 7.5 kg toroids, 3× contactors)?
Does the WB500 / P35 have N-PE (PEN-fault) monitoring, phase-sequence detection and an RDC-DD 6 mA? Their documented thresholds should be printed on the HMI 'expected reaction' field.
What is the supply earthing system at the demo venue (TN-C-S with PEN split in the building vs TN-S)? It affects whether the 'touch voltage on PE' demo can reference true earth.
Is an AFDD demo wanted? If yes a separate carbonised-cable arc generator per IEC 62606 is needed; the SSR chopper will not trip an AFDD.
